land.text: the Naiman country, over which the Kara-Khitans were sovereign until 1175

predecessors.note: The Naimans 'were subservient to them until 1175'; the page gives no date for the start of the subservience.

land.text: the Naiman country, absorbed by Temujin after the battle of 1204

successors.note: Cliopatria's Mongol Empire row begins in 1206; Temujin's Mongols held the land 1204-1206. The Naiman prince Kuchlug fled west to the Kara-Khitans and later usurped their throne (kara-khitans dossier, 1211).

correction.text: the Altai and western Mongolia from the Irtysh to the Tamir River

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. Page: 'the Naiman Khanate's western border reached the Irtysh River and its eastern border reached the Mongolian Tamir River' (Aristov's view); 'The Altai Mountains and southern Altai Republic were part of the Naiman Khanate'; 'originated in the territory of modern Western Mongolia'. Tayang's horde 'was living around the shores of the Black Irtysh' (Tayang Khan page) and met the Mongols in the Khangai Mountains and on the Orkhon in 1204. The page has no infobox area and no capital.

region.text: the Altai and western Mongolia from the Irtysh to the Tamir River

ledger.note: 1175: the Naimans cease to be subject to the Kara-Khitans. 'They had diplomatic relations with the Kara-Khitans, and were subservient to them until 1175.' The page dates no earlier formation ('thought to have emerged possibly during the period of the Uyghur Khaganate') and does not say what happened in 1175.

region.text: the Altai and western Mongolia from the Irtysh to the Tamir River

ledger.note: 1199: Temujin and Ong Khan attack the Naimans. 'In 1199, Temüjin (Genghis Khan) together with an ally Ong khan launched a campaign against the Naimans.' The page names no ground; the Naiman country is the zone.

region.text: the Altai and western Mongolia from the Irtysh to the Tamir River

ledger.note: 17 May 1204: Tayang Khan is beaten in the Khangai Mountains. 'The armies first met on 17 May 1204 in the Khangai Mountains'; Tayang crossed the Orkhon the next day; 'Tayang himself was killed whilst attempting to escape.'

region.text: the Altai and western Mongolia from the Irtysh to the Tamir River

ledger.note: 1204: the Naiman state ends. Kuchlug 'managed to escape and with a few Naiman soldiers fled westward towards the Kara Irtysh'; 'The rest of the tribe surrendered to Temujin and were absorbed into his ranks.' The Kuchlug page lists 'Khan of Naimans' 1204-1218 in its infobox, but no land is held by that remnant in any page opened.

wars.name: Mongol-Naiman war (Battle of Chakirmaut)

zones.text: the Khangai Mountains and the Orkhon

wars.outcome: Tayang Khan, joined by Jamukha, the Merkit chief Toqtoqa and the Oirat Quduqa, met Temujin on 17 May 1204 in the Khangai Mountains and was killed; the Naiman tribe was absorbed by the Mongols; Kuchlug fled west.
wars.note: The Tayang Khan page also has the Naiman approach to the Ongud in 1203 (Alaqush Tegin warned Genghis).

wars.name: Pursuit of Kuchlug
wars.outcome: After a second defeat Kuchlug was pushed 'further west into Zhetysu' in 1208 and turned to the Qara Khitai; he usurped their throne in 1211 and was pursued by Jebe from 1216 to 1218 (the kara-khitans dossier carries the Qara Khitai side).

certainty.note: A steppe khanate: the only description of its extent is a historian's view (Irtysh to the Tamir, Altai).

sources.title: Naimans
sources.note: Location and extent (Irtysh to the Tamir, Altai); subservient to the Kara-Khitans until 1175; 1199 campaign; 1203 Tayang killed; Kuchlug's flight.

sources.title: Kuchlug
sources.note: Kuchlug's flight to the Kara Irtysh, Zhetysu 1208, the throne of the Qara Khitai 1211, Jebe 1216-1218; Naiman remnant.

sources.title: Tayang Khan
sources.note: Reign c. 1198-1204; the Black Irtysh; Khangai 17 May 1204; Orkhon; death.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Naiman). The page gives no formation date, so the dossier starts in 1175 (end of Kara-Khitan sovereignty) and the earlier vassal period (ia-01-g counterparts: 1100-1218) is undated: the kara-khitans dossier does not carry the Naiman as a vassal, and a gap-filler may add it. The three pages disagree on the end: the Naimans page says 1203 for Tayang's death, the Tayang Khan page 1204 (the dossier uses 1204, with the Chakirmaut battle dated 17 May 1204 by the Tayang Khan page); Kuchlug is listed as 'Khan of Naimans 1204-1218' in the Kuchlug infobox but holds no land in the pages opened (he became the Qara Khitai usurper in 1211, a rename in the kara-khitans dossier). Cliopatria's Mongol Empire begins in 1206, so 1204-1206 is a gap in the successor row. The extent (Irtysh to the Tamir) is one historian's view (Aristov) cited by the page. Keraits and Merkits (also named in the group's scope) were not written: their pages were not opened. Gazetteer names used (Western Mongolia, Altai, Arhangay) all resolve.
